title: A gamified AI movement assessment and feedback approach for university students in physical education - Effects on movement skills, learning engagement, and behavioral patterns

segments.sourceText: Abstract University physical education courses often face challenges in sustaining students’ learning engagement, particularly when practice tasks feel repetitive, progress is hard to perceive, and there is a lack of personalized feedback based on individual students’ immediate performance. Although AI (Artificial Intelligence)-based movement assessment can help address the need for instant, individualized feedback, maintaining students’ engagement over time remains a persistent challenge. In response, we developed a gamified AI movement assessment and feedback (G-AI-MAF) approach based on the ARCS motivational model (i.e., Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction), and adopted a quasi-experimental design to explore the impact of gamification mechanisms, such as levels, experience points, leaderboards, and player data, on student learning. The participants consisted of 80 students from two yogism classes at a university. One class served as the experimental group, adopting the G-AI-MAF approach, while the other class served as the control group, adopting the conventional AI movement assessment and feedback (C-AI-MAF) approach. The results showed that the G-AI-MAF approach significantly improved students’ yogism movement skills performance and learning engagement. In terms of behavioral patterns, the experimental group took tests and checked results more frequently than the control group. These findings suggest that the gamification mechanism motivated students to engage in learning, significantly enhancing their active learning behaviors and the depth of system usage.

segments.sourceText: In physical education (PE), students’ movement skills performance serves as a key indicator for assessing teaching effectiveness. Enhancing students’ movement skills requires fostering their understanding of relevant theoretical knowledge and ensuring their proper execution of movements. Additionally, it is imperative to minimize incorrect practice to prevent potential sports injuries and declines in performance, ultimately achieving the educational goal of skill improvement. However, providing personalized guidance tailored to each student’s individual needs presents significant challenges for teachers (Chao et al., 2021; Yan & Cardinal, 2013; Yan & FitzPatrick, 2016). As a consequence, scholars have introduced technology-assisted learning, which has successfully demonstrated its effectiveness in terms of supporting PE courses (Almusawi et al., 2021; Moon et al., 2023). In particular, the application of artificial intelligence (AI) has opened up more opportunities for technology-assisted learning and personalized guidance (Chen et al., 2022; Lai & Tu, 2024; Tu & Lu, 2025). For example, AI speech recognition technology can instantly translate and assist students in learning languages (Darvishi et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023). Motion capture technology can analyze students’ movement skills performance and provide personalized guidance based on individual learning progress and challenges (Hsia et al., 2024, 2025; Li et al., 2024; Song, 2024). These studies have indicated that the personalized feedback provided by AI can indeed help most students learn more efficiently. However, some students have reported difficulties in understanding the learning performance analysis provided by AI, suggesting that they require additional support to fully comprehend their issues (Liu et al., 2024; Song, 2024; Wang et al., 2023). To address this issue, some scholars have suggested providing a visualized learning analytics dashboard that presents key indicators through simple charts, helping students understand and reflect on their learning process (Lee & Kim, 2024). In line with this recommendation, this study presented assessment results in a visualized format to assist students in overcoming language barriers and in understanding movement skills guidance.

segments.sourceText: On the other hand, students’ learning engagement and behavioral patterns are crucial factors for enhancing learning outcomes (Nair, 2022; Xiao & Hew, 2024). Therefore, promoting students’ learning engagement and fostering more proactive learning behaviors are significant teaching challenges. In response, many scholars have advocated for the application of gamified learning strategies to motivate students to learn (Dehghanzadeh et al., 2024; Saleem et al., 2022). Gamified learning refers to integrating game elements such as leaderboards, badges, and challenges into non-game learning environments. Numerous studies have reported the effects of gamification on motivating students to learn, thus enhancing their learning participation (Chen & Chen, 2023; Nair, 2022; Xiao & Hew, 2024). The benefits of gamification in fostering more active learning engagement are also evident in students’ learning behaviors. For example, well-designed gamified learning can encourage students to try different strategies to solve the challenges they face in learning tasks (Chou et al., 2023; Shang et al., 2024). Additionally, gamification helps students focus more on the learning topic, effectively reducing distractions during the learning process (Chang et al., 2024). Overall, gamified learning contributes to motivating students’ learning engagement and developing more proactive learning behaviors.

segments.sourceText: To ensure that gamification effectively enhances student learning, scholars have suggested designing gamified elements based on the ARCS motivational model (Camacho-Sánchez et al., 2023; Hao, 2023; Khan et al., 2022). Proposed by Keller (1987), the ARCS model comprises four dimensions: Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction. It emphasizes capturing students’ attention, attracting their interest through novel and engaging content, and helping them focus on developing core competencies related to their learning goals. Enhancing relevance involves strengthening the connection between learning content and students’ experiences, interests, and objectives to increase their perception of its practical value. The model also supports building students’ confidence by setting clear goals, introducing progressively challenging tasks, and providing positive feedback, fostering their belief in their ability to succeed. Finally, it reinforces satisfaction by offering a sense of achievement when students complete learning tasks, leveraging both external rewards and intrinsic fulfillment to create a positive reinforcement loop (Khan et al., 2022; Quadir et al., 2023). Existing research has demonstrated that gamified learning based on the ARCS model can yield positive learning outcomes in higher education PE courses (e.g., Camacho-Sánchez et al., 2023). However, the integration of AI-supported real-time visual learning analytics to assist students in acquiring movement skills remains an unexplored area, with the specific implementation strategies and learning benefits requiring further investigation.

However, the large-class format commonly adopted in PE courses often makes individualized instruction challenging, particularly in teaching movement skills. Chiang et al. (2019) found that personalized instruction tailored to specific skills could significantly enhance students’ performance, although it required more teaching resources.

This implied that students were particularly focused on receiving immediate feedback after completing the test, which contributed to improving their learning outcomes (Shang et al., 2024). The game elements effectively increased students’ interest in learning, helping them to take tests more frequently and to actively check the results (Chou et al., 2023; Shang et al., 2024). segments.sourceText: This study integrated the ARCS motivational model, which includes Attention, Relevance, Confidence, and Satisfaction, to ensure that the system effectively met the diverse psychological needs of students while offering gamified interactions. Students were more likely to repeatedly use the system due to specific applications of the ARCS model, such as using visual feedback to capture their attention, designing tasks that align with their life experiences to increase relevance, enhancing their confidence through immediate reward mechanisms, and boosting learning satisfaction through a sense of accomplishment upon task completion. This, in turn, promoted their active learning and improved their movement skills, leading to deeper learning engagement. The results of this study align with those of Camacho-Sánchez et al. (2023), Hao (2023), and Lin and Hou (2024), which indicated that integrating the ARCS motivational model into gamified learning systems could significantly enhance students’ engagement and active participation in learning. segments.sourceText: Despite its contributions, the limitations of the present study should also be acknowledged. That is, the sample comprised students from a single institution in a specified course taught by the same instructor. Although this design was intended to control for teacher variability and ensure internal validity, it potentially limits the representativeness and external validity of the findings. It is suggested that future research validate the G-AI-MAF approach across diverse institutions and encompass a broader range of nationalities to enhance generalizability. Furthermore, as this study focused solely on yogism, future studies could extend the application to various types of physical activities and explore the integration of different game elements with AI technologies to further investigate their effectiveness.

abstract.faithfulZh: 背景 身體活動 (PA) 對身心健康至關重要，但許多大學生未能達到推薦的水平。 透過移動應用程式進行的人工智慧（AI）驅動的遊戲化干預有可能提高中國大學生的 PA 水平。 目的 本研究旨在評估 AI 驅動的遊戲化干預的可行性和可用性。 方法對北京18所大學18-25歲大學生進行了跨2個月的準實驗研究。 PA 資料是使用 Shouti Fitness 應用程式記錄的，並透過調查評估參與者的參與度。 透過系統可用性量表來衡量使用者滿意度，而透過 Spearman 等級相關分析、Mann-Whitney 測試和其他描述性分析來評估干預的可行性。 結果 截至 2023 年 7 月，我們招收了 456 名大學生。 總共記錄了 18,073 次 PA 課程，男性完成了 8068 次會議，女性完成了 10,055 次會議。 平均 PA 強度為每個會話的 7 個代謝當量能量 (MET)。 大多數參與者更喜歡下午的會議和喜歡的短期會議，男性平均每節 66 秒，女性 42 秒。 基於 APP 的干預系統可用性量表評分為 65.2。 使用者對 AI 和遊戲化元素的整合做出了積極響應，包括個性化推薦、動作識別、智慧分組、動態管理、協作和競爭。 具體來說，341 名使用者 (75%) 發現 AI 功能非常有趣，365 人 (80%) 受到遊戲化元素的激勵，364 人 (80%) 表示干預支援他們的健身目標，365 人 (80%) 認為干預措施可靠。 儘管女性的相關性較弱（ρ=0.258，p =.046），但個體 PA 的持續時間和男性干預持續時間之間存在顯著的正相關（ρ=0.510，p <.001）。 然而，PA 的頻率在 35 天后下降。 結論 本研究為 AI 驅動的遊戲化干預的可行性和可用性提供了開創性的證據。 雖然成功證明了依從性，但需要進一步的研究或干預措施來直接評估對 PA 水平的影響，並專注於最佳化長期依從策略和評估健康結果。

abstract.faithfulZh: 作為第二語言 (L2) 寫作課堂中的一項重要學習活動，同伴回饋在提高學生的寫作能力方面發揮著至關重要的作用。 然而，學生審稿人在對同行的論文提供有影響力的回饋方面面臨挑戰。 低品質的同行評審成為一個持續存在的問題，對同行回饋的學習效果產生不利影響。 為了加強學生的同行回饋提供，本研究引入了 AI 支援的同行評審系統 Evaluate，該系統包含一個名為 EVA 的聊天機器人，旨在評估和提供對學生審稿人對同行論文評論的評論的回饋。 44 名中國本科生參與評估，利用其特徵對同行的英語辯論論文產生回饋。 收集了捕獲學生與聊天機器人互動的聊天記錄資料，包括他們對同伴論文發表的評論以及聊天機器人對他們評論的回饋。 結果表明，人工智慧監管的整合提高了學生同行評審的品質。 學生在評論修訂期間採用各種策略來響應 AI 回饋，例如引入新點、新增細節和提供說明性示例，這有助於提高他們的評論品質。 這些發現揭示了 AI 支援的同行評審系統在授權學生提供有關同行的書面工作的更有價值的回饋方面的好處。 從業者筆記 學者們已經廣泛研究了不同的教學策略，以提高學生在第二語言 (L2) 寫作課堂中的同伴回饋提供技能。 人工智慧 (AI) 技術已被用於監控和評估學生審閱者產生的同行回饋。 支援 AI 的同行回饋評估工具已經證明了對學生審稿人同行回饋提供有效評估的能力。 本文在 L2 寫作的背景下補充了什麼，缺乏定製的 AI 同行回饋評估工具。 為了解決這一差距，我們開發了一個 AI 支援的同行評審系統 Evaluate，它包含一個名為 EVA 的大型基於語言模型的聊天機器人。 EVA 旨在就 L2 學生對同齡人寫作的評論提供回饋。 雖然以前的研究主要集中在評估支援 AI 的同行回饋評估工具的有效性上，但人們對學生如何將 AI 支援整合到改進同行評審評論中知之甚少。 為了彌合這一差距，我們的研究不僅考察了使用該系統（評估）是否可以提高 L2 學生同行評審評論的品質，還要檢查學生在修改評論時如何回應 EVA 的回饋。 對實踐和/或政策的影響 開發 AI 支援的同行評審系統（Evalualume）為二語寫作教師引入了一種創新的教學方法，以培訓和提高學生的同行回饋供應技能。 將 AI 監督整合到 L2 學生的同行回饋生成中，可以提高學生審稿人對其同行寫作的評論品質。 學生在修改評論以回應 EVA 的回饋時採用各種策略，這些策略導致評論品質的不同程度改進。 L2 寫作教師可以向學生教授有效的修訂策略。

abstract.faithfulZh: 遊戲化通常以數字方式實現。 然而，由於資源有限和後勤問題，數字遊戲化並不總是可能的。 因此，有必要探索可以在課堂上輕鬆採用的低閾值遊戲化方法。 一種這樣的方法是使用物理遊戲設計元素的非數字遊戲化。 目前，文獻對非數字遊戲化的設計和效果提供了有限的理解。 還不清楚混合遊戲化（即數字遊戲和非數字遊戲化的組合）是否優於純非數字遊戲化。 我們使用解釋性順序混合方法設計來探索這些主題，以比較非數字遊戲化在面對面課程中的有效性，並在學生學習成績、認知參與度和課程滿意度方面進行混合課程中的混合遊戲化的有效性。 兩個中學年級被隨機分配到混合 (n = 52) 或非數字 (n = 52) 遊戲化條件。 與我們的預期相反，定量結果表明，這兩種方法在相同程度上提高了學生的學習成績。 儘管非數字遊戲化條件下的學生報告的課程滿意度明顯高於混合條件下的學生，但混合遊戲化條件下的學生認知參與度的改善明顯高於非數字條件。 透過焦點小組訪談，我們分析了學生的學習經歷，並綜合了影響學生認知參與度和課程滿意度的因素。 從業者注意，關於這個主題的已知內容越來越多地被用於增加學生的參與度和增強學習。 遊戲化研究主要集中在數字模式上，這些模式通常需要遊戲化的數字平臺或應用程式。 非數字遊戲化可以是促進學習的有效方法，但非數字遊戲化的設計和評估還處於早期階段。 本文補充說，我們設計了非數字和混合（即數字和非數字）遊戲化程式，並使用解釋性順序混合方法設計比較了它們的效果。 兩種遊戲化方法都在學習成績方面取得了類似的進步。 雖然非數字遊戲化提高了學生的課程滿意度，但混合遊戲化在提高學生的認知參與方面更有效。 對實踐和/或政策非數字遊戲化的影響對於教師來說可能是一種有效的低閾值解決方案。 值得進一步改進學校環境中的非數字遊戲化方法，因為它具有成本效益，並且可以在課堂之間轉移。 混合遊戲化的好處不應被忽視，因為它的可供性可以提高學生的認知參與度。

explanationRepairs.sourceText: In physical education (PE), students’ movement skills performance serves as a key indicator for assessing teaching effectiveness. Enhancing students’ movement skills requires fostering their understanding of relevant theoretical knowledge and ensuring their proper execution of movements. Additionally, it is imperative to minimize incorrect practice to prevent potential sports injuries and declines in performance, ultimately achieving the educational goal of skill improvement. However, providing personalized guidance tailored to each student’s individual needs presents significant challenges for teachers (Chao et al., 2021; Yan & Cardinal, 2013; Yan & FitzPatrick, 2016). As a consequence, scholars have introduced technology-assisted learning, which has successfully demonstrated its effectiveness in terms of supporting PE courses (Almusawi et al., 2021; Moon et al., 2023). In particular, the application of artificial intelligence (AI) has opened up more opportunities for technology-assisted learning and personalized guidance (Chen et al., 2022; Lai & Tu, 2024; Tu & Lu, 2025). For example, AI speech recognition technology can instantly translate and assist students in learning languages (Darvishi et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023).
